parts.title: Léctio sancti Evangélii secúndum Matthǽum
paragraphs: In illo témpore: Defúncto Heróde, ecce, Angelus Dómini appáruit in somnis Joseph in Ægýpto, dicens: Surge, et áccipe Púerum et Matrem ejus, et vade in terram Israël: defúncti sunt enim, qui quærébant ánimam Pueri. Qui consúrgens, accépit Púerum et Matrem ejus, et venit in terram Israël. Audiens autem, quod Archeláus regnáret in Judæa pro Heróde patre suo, tímuit illo ire: et, admonítus in somnis, secéssit in partes Galilææ. Et véniens habitávit in civitáte, quæ vocátur Názareth: ut adimplére tur quod dictum est per Prophétas: Quóniam Nazaræus vocábitur.

parts.title: Homilía sancti Hierónymi Presbýteri
parts.source: Liber 1 in Comment. in cap. 2 Matthæi
paragraphs: Ex hoc loco intellígimus non solum Heródem, sed et sacerdótes et scribas eódem témpore necem Dómini fuísse meditátos. Qui surgens accépit púerum, et matrem ejus. Non dixit: Accépit fílium suum et uxórem suam, sed Púerum et matrem ejus; quasi nutrítius, non marítus.

responsory.text: Nésciens Mater Virgo virum, péperit sine dolóre Salvatórem sæculórum.
responsory.repeat: Ipsum Regem Angelórum, sola Virgo lactábat úbere de cælo pleno.

responsory.text: Beáta víscera Maríæ Vírginis, quæ portavérunt ætérni Patris Fílium. (Allelúja.)
Ipsum Regem Angelórum, sola Virgo lactábat úbere de cælo pleno.

parts.title: From the Holy Gospel according to Matthew
paragraphs: In that time: When Herod was dead, behold an angel of the Lord appeared in sleep to Joseph in Egypt, Saying: Arise, and take the child and his mother, and go into the land of Israel. For they are dead that sought the life of the child. Who arose, and took the child and his mother, and came into the land of Israel. But hearing that Archclaus reigned in Judea in the room of Herod his father, he was afraid to go thither: and being warned in sleep retired into the quarters of Galilee. And coming he dwelt in a city called Nazareth: that it might be fulfilled which was said by the prophets: That he shall be called a Nazarene.

parts.title: Homily by St. Jerome, Priest (at Bethlehem.)
parts.source: Bk. i., Comm. on Matth. ii.
paragraphs: From the words, they are dead, (in the Plural), which are used in this passage of the Gospel, we may understand that there were others beside Herod which sought the young Child's life probably the Priests and Scribes. And he Joseph arose, and took the young Child and His Mother. It is not written, He took his wife and child, but he took the young Child and His Mother; whence it is clear that the holy Evangelist willeth to imply that Joseph was not the father, but the Guardian of Jesus, not the husband, but the Betrothed of Mary.

responsory.text: Nésciens Mater Virgo virum, péperit sine dolóre Salvatórem sæculórum.
responsory.repeat: Ipsum Regem Angelórum, sola Virgo lactábat úbere de cælo pleno.

responsory.text: Blessed is the womb of the Virgin Mary, which bore the Son of the eternal Father.
Ipsum Regem Angelórum, sola Virgo lactábat úbere de cælo pleno.

paragraphs: Audiens autem quod Archeláus regnáret in Judǽa pro Heróde patre suo, tímuit illo ire. Multi labúntur erróre propter ignorántiam históriæ, putántes eumdem esse Heródem, a quo in passióne sua Dóminus irridétur, et qui nunc mórtuus esse referátur. Ergo Heródes ille qui cum Piláto póstea amicítias fecit, hujus Heródis fílius est, frater Archelái.

responsory.text: Confirmátum est cor Vírginis, in quo divína mystéria, Angelo nuntiánte, concépit: tunc speciósum forma præ fíliis hóminum castis suscépit viscéribus:
responsory.repeat: Et benedícta in ætérnum, Deum nobis prótulit et hóminem.

responsory.text: Domus pudíci péctoris templum repénte fit Dei: intácta nésciens virum, verbo concépit Fílium.
Et benedícta in ætérnum, Deum nobis prótulit et hóminem.

paragraphs: But when he heard that Archelaus did reign in Judea, in the room of his father Herod, he was afraid to go thither. There are some persons so grossly ignorant of history that they confuse themselves over the two Herods, as if the one mentioned here were the same who afterwards set our Lord at nought during His Passion, and they cannot understand how he should now be said to be dead. The Herod who was made friends with Pilate over Christ's death, was the son of the Herod who massacred the infants of Bethlehem, and the brother of Archelaus.

responsory.text: The heart of the Virgin was fixed, when the Angel declared unto her the mystery of God, and she conceived, then did she receive in her pure womb Him That is fairer than the children of men.
responsory.repeat: And, she that is blessed for ever, brought forth for us God and man.

responsory.text: Soon rises, in that modest shrine, The Temple of the Lord Divine The stainless and unwedded one, Within her womb conceived the Son.
And, she that is blessed for ever, brought forth for us God and man.

paragraphs: Quóniam Nazarǽus vocábitur. Si fixum de Scriptúris posuísset exémplum, numquam díceret: Quod dictum est per prophétas: sed simplíciter: Quod dictum est per prophétam. Nunc autem pluráliter prophétas vocans, osténdit se non verba de Scriptúris sumpsísse, sed sensum. interpretátur; sanctum autem Dóminum futúrum omnis Scriptúra commémorat.

responsory.text: O Regem cæli, cui talia famulántur obsequia: stábulo pónitur, qui cóntinet mundum:
responsory.repeat: Jacet in præsépio, et in cælis regnat.

responsory.text: Natus est nobis hódie Salvator, qui est Christus Dóminus, in civitáte David.
Jacet in præsépio, et in cælis regnat.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
Jacet in præsépio, et in cælis regnat.

If he had been citing any one precise passage he would have said by the Prophet, in the Singular. But he is citing the sense of the Prophets, and not any individual passage in any of their writings. He seemeth to refer to the fact that in Hebrew the word Nazarene signifieth holy, and that Christ is the Holy One of God is the common declaration of all the Scriptures.

responsory.text: How is the King of heaven attended? He that containeth the world is laid in a stable;
responsory.repeat: Lying in a manger, reigning in heaven.

responsory.text: Unto us is born, this day, in the city of David, a Saviour, Which is Christ the Lord.
Lying in a manger, reigning in heaven.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

latin.heading: Octávo Idus Januárii Luna vicésima octáva. Anno Dómini 2027
entries: Floréntiæ natális sancti Andréæ Corsíni, civis Florentíni, ex Ordine Carmelitárum, Epíscopi Fesuláni et Confessóris; quem, miráculis clarum, Urbánus Papa Octávus in Sanctórum númerum rétulit. Ejus autem festívitas recólitur prídie Nonas Februárii.
Barcinóne, in Hispánia, item natális sancti Raymúndi de Peñáfort, ex Ordine Prædicatórum, Confessóris, doctrína et sanctitáte célebris. Ipsíus vero festum décimo Kaléndas Februárii celebrátur.
In Africa commemorátio plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum, qui, in persecutióne Sevéri, ad palum ligáti sunt et igne consúmpti.

In território Rheménsi pássio sanctæ Macræ Vírginis, quæ, in persecutióne Diocletiáni, jubénte Rictiováro Prǽside, cum in ignem esset præcipitáta et permansísset illǽsa, dehinc, mamíllis abscíssis et squalóre cárceris afflícta, super testas étiam acutíssimas ac prunas volutáta, tandem orans migrávit ad Dóminum.
Rhédonis, in Gállia, sancti Melánii, Epíscopi et Confessóris; qui, post innumerabílium signa virtútum, júgiter cælo inténtus, gloriósus migrávit a sǽculo.
Geris, in Ægýpto, sancti Nilammónis reclúsi, qui, dum ad Episcopátum traherétur invítus, in oratióne spíritum Deo réddidit.
latin.closing: Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.

translation.heading: January 6th 2027, the 28th day of the Moon
entries: The morrow is the Epiphany of the Lord.
Upon the same 6th day of January, were born into the better life:

At Florence, holy Andrew Corsini of that city, a Carmelite friar, Bishop of Fiesoli, who was famous for miracles (in the year 1373), and whose name was numbered by Urban VIII. among those of the Saints, whose feast we keep upon the 4th day of February.

At Barcelona (in the year 1275), holy Raymond of Pehafuerte, of the order of Friars Preachers, famous for his holiness and teaching, whose feast we keep upon the 23rd day of this present month of January.
On the same day are commemorated many holy martyrs in Africa, who were burnt at the stake in the persecution under the Emperor Severus.

In the country of Reims, by command of the President Rictiovarus, in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian, the holy virgin and martyr Macra she was first cast into the fire but remained unhurt, whereupon her breasts were cut off, and she was thrust into a prison and rolled upon sharp potsherds and live coals until she passed away in prayer to be ever with the Lord.

At Rennes, in Gaul, the holy confessor Melanius (Abbot of Platz) (in the year 511), bishop of that see, who after countless works of power passed gloriously out of this world to that heaven where his heart was already fixed (in the year 530).
At Geris, in Egypt, the holy hermit Nilammon, who gave up his soul in prayer to God while he was being haled against his will to make him a bishop (fifth century).
translation.closing: And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.

Matins · Tuesday, 5 January 2027

Vigil of the Epiphany

In Vigilia Epiphaniæ · Semiduplex

Commemoration: St. Telesphorus, Pope and Martyr

Read in Latin and English{{listen}}

Lesson I

From the Holy Gospel according to Matthew

Matt 2:19-23

In that time: When Herod was dead, behold an angel of the Lord appeared in sleep to Joseph in Egypt, Saying: Arise, and take the child and his mother, and go into the land of Israel. For they are dead that sought the life of the child. Who arose, and took the child and his mother, and came into the land of Israel. But hearing that Archclaus reigned in Judea in the room of Herod his father, he was afraid to go thither: and being warned in sleep retired into the quarters of Galilee. And coming he dwelt in a city called Nazareth: that it might be fulfilled which was said by the prophets: That he shall be called a Nazarene.

Homily by St. Jerome, Priest (at Bethlehem.)

Bk. i., Comm. on Matth. ii.

From the words, they are dead, (in the Plural), which are used in this passage of the Gospel, we may understand that there were others beside Herod which sought the young Child's life probably the Priests and Scribes. And he Joseph arose, and took the young Child and His Mother. It is not written, He took his wife and child, but he took the young Child and His Mother; whence it is clear that the holy Evangelist willeth to imply that Joseph was not the father, but the Guardian of Jesus, not the husband, but the Betrothed of Mary.

℟. Nésciens Mater Virgo virum, péperit sine dolóre Salvatórem sæculórum. * Ipsum Regem Angelórum, sola Virgo lactábat úbere de cælo pleno.

℣. Blessed is the womb of the Virgin Mary, which bore the Son of the eternal Father.

℟. Ipsum Regem Angelórum, sola Virgo lactábat úbere de cælo pleno.

Lesson II

But when he heard that Archelaus did reign in Judea, in the room of his father Herod, he was afraid to go thither. There are some persons so grossly ignorant of history that they confuse themselves over the two Herods, as if the one mentioned here were the same who afterwards set our Lord at nought during His Passion, and they cannot understand how he should now be said to be dead. The Herod who was made friends with Pilate over Christ's death, was the son of the Herod who massacred the infants of Bethlehem, and the brother of Archelaus.

℟. The heart of the Virgin was fixed, when the Angel declared unto her the mystery of God, and she conceived, then did she receive in her pure womb Him That is fairer than the children of men. * And, she that is blessed for ever, brought forth for us God and man.

℣. Soon rises, in that modest shrine, The Temple of the Lord Divine The stainless and unwedded one, Within her womb conceived the Son.

℟. And, she that is blessed for ever, brought forth for us God and man.

Lesson III

He shall be called a Nazarene. The Evangelist, in quoting these words, saith that they were spoken by the Prophets, (Plural). If he had been citing any one precise passage he would have said by the Prophet, in the Singular. But he is citing the sense of the Prophets, and not any individual passage in any of their writings. He seemeth to refer to the fact that in Hebrew the word Nazarene signifieth holy, and that Christ is the Holy One of God is the common declaration of all the Scriptures.

℟. How is the King of heaven attended? He that containeth the world is laid in a stable; * Lying in a manger, reigning in heaven.

℣. Unto us is born, this day, in the city of David, a Saviour, Which is Christ the Lord.

℟. Lying in a manger, reigning in heaven.

℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

℟. Lying in a manger, reigning in heaven.

Martyrology

Read at Prime today, announcing tomorrow

January 6th 2027, the 28th day of the Moon

The morrow is the Epiphany of the Lord.

Upon the same 6th day of January, were born into the better life:

At Florence, holy Andrew Corsini of that city, a Carmelite friar, Bishop of Fiesoli, who was famous for miracles (in the year 1373), and whose name was numbered by Urban VIII. among those of the Saints, whose feast we keep upon the 4th day of February.

At Barcelona (in the year 1275), holy Raymond of Pehafuerte, of the order of Friars Preachers, famous for his holiness and teaching, whose feast we keep upon the 23rd day of this present month of January.

On the same day are commemorated many holy martyrs in Africa, who were burnt at the stake in the persecution under the Emperor Severus.

In the country of Reims, by command of the President Rictiovarus, in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian, the holy virgin and martyr Macra she was first cast into the fire but remained unhurt, whereupon her breasts were cut off, and she was thrust into a prison and rolled upon sharp potsherds and live coals until she passed away in prayer to be ever with the Lord.

At Rennes, in Gaul, the holy confessor Melanius (Abbot of Platz) (in the year 511), bishop of that see, who after countless works of power passed gloriously out of this world to that heaven where his heart was already fixed (in the year 530).

At Geris, in Egypt, the holy hermit Nilammon, who gave up his soul in prayer to God while he was being haled against his will to make him a bishop (fifth century).

℣. And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.

℟. Thanks be to God.

Read in Latin and English

Cistercian Breviary, 1951. Texts from Divinum Officium (divinumofficium.com).

If he had been citing any one precise passage he would have said by the Prophet, in the Singular. But he is citing the sense of the Prophets, and not any individual passage in any of their writings. He seemeth to refer to the fact that in Hebrew the word Nazarene signifieth holy, and that Christ is the Holy One of God is the common declaration of all the Scriptures.

℟. O Regem cæli, cui talia famulántur obsequia: stábulo pónitur, qui cóntinet mundum: * Jacet in præsépio, et in cælis regnat.

℟. How is the King of heaven attended? He that containeth the world is laid in a stable; * Lying in a manger, reigning in heaven.

℣. Natus est nobis hódie Salvator, qui est Christus Dóminus, in civitáte David.

℣. Unto us is born, this day, in the city of David, a Saviour, Which is Christ the Lord.

℟. Jacet in præsépio, et in cælis regnat.

℟. Lying in a manger, reigning in heaven.

℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

Epiphánia Dómini.

Floréntiæ natális sancti Andréæ Corsíni, civis Florentíni, ex Ordine Carmelitárum, Epíscopi Fesuláni et Confessóris; quem, miráculis clarum, Urbánus Papa Octávus in Sanctórum númerum rétulit. Ejus autem festívitas recólitur prídie Nonas Februárii.

Barcinóne, in Hispánia, item natális sancti Raymúndi de Peñáfort, ex Ordine Prædicatórum, Confessóris, doctrína et sanctitáte célebris. Ipsíus vero festum décimo Kaléndas Februárii celebrátur.

In Africa commemorátio plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum, qui, in persecutióne Sevéri, ad palum ligáti sunt et igne consúmpti.

In território Rheménsi pássio sanctæ Macræ Vírginis, quæ, in persecutióne Diocletiáni, jubénte Rictiováro Prǽside, cum in ignem esset præcipitáta et permansísset illǽsa, dehinc, mamíllis abscíssis et squalóre cárceris afflícta, super testas étiam acutíssimas ac prunas volutáta, tandem orans migrávit ad Dóminum.

Rhédonis, in Gállia, sancti Melánii, Epíscopi et Confessóris; qui, post innumerabílium signa virtútum, júgiter cælo inténtus, gloriósus migrávit a sǽculo.

Geris, in Ægýpto, sancti Nilammónis reclúsi, qui, dum ad Episcopátum traherétur invítus, in oratióne spíritum Deo réddidit.

℣. Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.

January 6th 2027, the 28th day of the Moon

The morrow is the Epiphany of the Lord.

Upon the same 6th day of January, were born into the better life:

At Florence, holy Andrew Corsini of that city, a Carmelite friar, Bishop of Fiesoli, who was famous for miracles (in the year 1373), and whose name was numbered by Urban VIII. among those of the Saints, whose feast we keep upon the 4th day of February.

At Barcelona (in the year 1275), holy Raymond of Pehafuerte, of the order of Friars Preachers, famous for his holiness and teaching, whose feast we keep upon the 23rd day of this present month of January.

On the same day are commemorated many holy martyrs in Africa, who were burnt at the stake in the persecution under the Emperor Severus.

In the country of Reims, by command of the President Rictiovarus, in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian, the holy virgin and martyr Macra she was first cast into the fire but remained unhurt, whereupon her breasts were cut off, and she was thrust into a prison and rolled upon sharp potsherds and live coals until she passed away in prayer to be ever with the Lord.

At Rennes, in Gaul, the holy confessor Melanius (Abbot of Platz) (in the year 511), bishop of that see, who after countless works of power passed gloriously out of this world to that heaven where his heart was already fixed (in the year 530).

At Geris, in Egypt, the holy hermit Nilammon, who gave up his soul in prayer to God while he was being haled against his will to make him a bishop (fifth century).

℣. And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
